title: Practice: an MCP server's side of a multi round-trip request (Java)

blocks.text: Practice: an MCP server's side of a multi round-trip request

In the MCP revision of 2026-07-28 a server no longer calls the client in the middle of a request. When a tool needs a person's answer or a model completion, it ends the call with an `input_required` result that lists what it needs, and the client retries the same call with the answers. The server keeps nothing between the two calls, so whatever it needs to remember travels in an opaque `requestState` that the client echoes back. That state crosses a client the server does not trust, so it must be signed, bound to the user and the call, and given an expiry. Write the tool handler that does this. The message shapes, the rules for `requestState`, the error codes and the capability checks come from the MCP specification of revision 2026-07-28 (the multi round-trip requests, tools, elicitation and sampling pages), read on 2026-10-03; the lesson pages explain them. Nothing here uses a network or an MCP SDK: the handler is a function from the parameters of a request to the result, which is what the SDKs call underneath.

rows: request

the parameters of a `tools/call`: `{"name", "arguments", "_meta", optionally "inputResponses" and "requestState"}`; `_meta` holds the protocol version under `io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion` and the capabilities the client declares under `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities`
`TOOLS`, `VERSION`, `TTL_SECONDS`
the two tool definitions (`deploy` and `status`), the one protocol version served, and the lifetime of a state: 300 seconds
`mint_state(secret, payload)`
a `requestState` for the payload, signed with the secret
`read_state(secret, token)`
the payload of a `requestState`, or nothing when it is not one this secret signed (changed, cut short, signed by another secret, or not a state at all)
`args_digest(arguments)`
a fingerprint of the arguments, the same in any key order

blocks.text: What is already written, and what you write

The starter is a working handler with eight gaps cut out of it. Everything that is plumbing is written and correct: the state signing (`mint_state`, `read_state`, `args_digest`), the error and result builders, the two request messages, the version check, and the order in which `call_tool` runs its steps. Each gap is a small function with its signature, a comment that says what it receives and returns with one example, and the cases it unlocks. A gap returns a neutral value, so the starter runs and fails the cases on an assertion. Debug a gap by logging its input with the `log` line at the top of the file; a run shows the lines under the failing case. Write them in this order (the Java, Kotlin and TypeScript names are the camel-case forms):

items: `_validate` unlocks `e6`: the protocol error for an unknown tool, a missing service or a bad env.
`_can_elicit` unlocks `e2`: which declared capabilities mean the client can be asked.
`_confirm_usable` unlocks `m1` and `e3`: which answers count as an answer to the question.
`_confirmed` unlocks `e3`: only an accept with `confirm` exactly true goes on.
`_notes_text` unlocks `m1`: the sentence the client wrote for the release notes.
`_state_error` unlocks `e4` and `e5`: the three checks on a returned state, in order.
`_new_state` unlocks `e7`: the payload that carries the whole context.
`_tool_listing` unlocks `e1`: the cacheable tool list.

blocks.text: About twenty lines in all. The sections below describe the whole handler; the parts you do not write are there so you can see how your functions are used.

items: `list_tools(request)`: a request whose version is not `VERSION` is a protocol error (below). Otherwise `{"resultType": "complete", "tools": TOOLS sorted by name, "ttlMs": 300000, "cacheScope": "public"}`.

`call_tool(request, secret, principal, now)` where `principal` is the authenticated user and `now` is the time in seconds. It returns a result, or a protocol error `{"error": {"code", "message", optionally "data"}}`. Check in this order:
Version not `VERSION`: code `-32022`, message `Unsupported protocol version`, `data` `{"supported": [VERSION]}`.
A tool name other than `deploy` and `status`: `-32602`, `Unknown tool: NAME`.

`arguments.service` missing, not a string or only spaces: `-32602`, `Invalid params: service is required`. For `deploy`, an `env` that is not `staging` or `production`: `-32602`, `Invalid params: env must be staging or production`.
`status` completes with the text `SERVICE: running`. `deploy` to `staging` completes with `Deployed SERVICE to staging`. Both need no input from the client.
A complete result is `{"resultType": "complete", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": ...}], "isError": false}`.

`deploy` to `production` needs a person's confirmation by elicitation. The client can be asked only when it declared an `elicitation` capability that is empty (which means form mode) or holds `form`; a capability with only `url`, or none, cannot be asked. Then the result is complete with `isError` true and the text `Deploying to production needs confirmation, and this client cannot be asked.` and nothing is requested.
Otherwise there are up to two steps, kept in the signed state, not in the server:

Step `confirm`: with no usable answer, return `{"resultType": "input_required", "inputRequests": {"confirm": ...}, "requestState": ...}`. The request is `{"method": "elicitation/create", "params": {"mode": "form", "message": "Deploy SERVICE to production?", "requestedSchema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"confirm": {"type": "boolean", "title": "Confirm the deployment"}}, "required": ["confirm"]}}}`. An answer is usable when `inputResponses.confirm` is an object whose `action` is `accept`, `decline` or `cancel`; anything else, or a missing answer, is asked again with a fresh state. Only `accept` with `content.confirm` exactly true goes on; every other usable answer completes with `Deployment cancelled` (and `isError` false). After a confirmation, a client that declared a `sampling` capability gets step `notes`; one that did not completes with `Deployed SERVICE to production`.

Step `notes`: ask with `{"notes": {"method": "sampling/createMessage", "params": {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": {"type": "text", "text": "Write one sentence of release notes for SERVICE."}}], "maxTokens": 100}}}`. The answer is usable when `inputResponses.notes.content.text` is a string; the result is then `Deployed SERVICE to production. Release notes: TEXT`. An unusable or missing answer is asked again.

The state payload is `{"v": 1, "tool", "digest": args_digest(arguments), "sub": principal, "exp": now + TTL_SECONDS, "step"}`; `step` is the step that the next call must answer (`confirm` or `notes`).

A call with no `requestState` starts at step `confirm` and ignores any `inputResponses`: an answer alone never skips the question. A call with a `requestState` is checked in this order, with code `-32602`: a state that `read_state` does not accept: `Invalid requestState`; `now` later than `exp`: `Expired requestState`; a `sub`, `tool` or `digest` that differs from this call: `requestState does not match this request`. A valid state sets the step. Unknown keys in `inputResponses` are ignored.
